repairs.title: atomic admission
repairs.root_cause: submitTask() called slotGate() and store.append() in two separate _withLock acquisitions, with the capacity decision taken outside both. Two processes could each observe a free slot and both append.
repairs.change: dedup decision, capacity decision and QUEUED append now all execute inside ONE store._withLock scope via the new _appendLocked primitive.

pre_hardening_evidence.note: the reviewer's claimed 2-admitted result was timing luck; this run reproduced the violation

independent_stress.note: written independently of the reviewer's harness

repairs.acceptance: N >> cap satisfied (24 processes against cap 2); many repeated trials (40, plus the reviewer's 8); admitted never exceeded cap; duplicate submission remained idempotent under contention.

repairs.title: un-droppable state transitions
repairs.root_cause: eventKey was task_id|attempt|seq and omitted state, so a legitimate advance that reused a sequence number was silently swallowed.
repairs.reproduction: QUEUED seq1, then RUNNING seq2 appended, then RETURNED seq2 returned {appended:false, dedup:true}; final states were [QUEUED, RUNNING].
repairs.change: sequence OWNERSHIP rather than key widening. nextSeqFor() computes a monotonic per-(task_id, attempt) sequence from the records already read under the writer lock; recordTaskEvent() is the supported entry point and the store allocates the sequence itself.
repairs.why_not_state_in_key: The commission warned that merely appending state to the key creates replay ambiguity. Under key-widening a buggy caller replaying one logical transition under a different state would produce two competing truths for a single attempt. Sequence ownership removes the collision without introducing that ambiguity.

repairs.title: no blanket --auto
repairs.root_cause: blanket --auto was required for any positive end-to-end run; the CLI self-labels it '(dangerous!)' and it auto-approves anything not explicitly denied.
repairs.change: --auto is now refused outright (GateError BLANKET_AUTO_REFUSED). A scoped permission profile is injected per-process through OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT, and OPENCODE_CONFIG is deleted from the child environment so no global config can widen permissions.

permission_surface_verified_on_installed.source: real config surface discovered in @opencode-ai/sdk types and confirmed by opencode debug config

acceptance_evidence.authorized_fixture_write_succeeds: real opencode run created out/allowed.txt containing ALLOWED_OK with no --auto
acceptance_evidence.out_of_terrain_denied_by_runtime_before_: runtime emitted permission=external_directory pattern=/tmp/.../OUTSIDE/* action.action=deny and the tool call failed with 'The user has specified a rule which prevents you from using this specific tool call'; no file created
acceptance_evidence.control_proves_the_permission_is_load_be: the IDENTICAL insisting prompt under external_directory:allow DID write the out-of-terrain file, so the denial under deny is the permission layer and not model reluctance
acceptance_evidence.dangerous_unrelated_access_denied: bash denied by pattern - the bash tool was not even offered to the session
acceptance_evidence.no_global_config_destructively_rewritten: per-process env only; OPENCODE_CONFIG removed from the child env; no file under ~/.config or ~/.local/share/opencode was modified by the dispatcher

repairs.title: process containment
repairs.finding: the prior review found no OS or process containment; the dispatcher was pure advisory and state law.
repairs.change: launch() now wraps the child in a macOS seatbelt (sandbox-exec) profile in which the ONLY writable locations are the task worktree, OpenCode's own session/cache dirs, and the lane scratch dir. Worktree separation is explicitly NOT claimed as containment.

acceptance_evidence.independent_of_application_permissions: with opencode configured fully permissively (external_directory:allow, bash:* allow) the kernel still refused the out-of-worktree write and the tool call physically failed
acceptance_evidence.honesty_probe: an early profile revision produced a FALSE PASS because the profile failed to compile; that was caught and corrected, and the profile now compiles before any result is claimed

repairs.host_safety_compliance: no sudo; no system, /etc, launch-agent or global security change; the seatbelt profile is a disposable lane-owned fixture applied only to the child under test; no ownership, ACL or recursive permission change anywhere.

repairs.title: commission delivery integrity
repairs.root_cause: the --file attachment channel renders attachment content as faux tool-call blocks, so commission text could be presented in the visual shape of an operator instruction.
repairs.change: two independent halves, because a hash alone cannot solve interpretation. INTEGRITY: sha256 of the exact bytes is computed before launch and compared to the bound identity; drift aborts with COMMISSION_DELIVERY_DRIFT. AUTHORITY: the governing instruction block is generated by the dispatcher from dispatcher-held values only and never from the commission, and it states an explicit precedence rule under which the entire attachment is DATA. The attached rendering additionally has faux tool-call markers defanged so the channel cannot present data in the shape of an instruction.
repairs.why_two_halves: binding bytes proves WHICH document was delivered; it does not stop the interpreter treating that document's contents as authority. The authority half is what actually removes the injection risk, and it is generated where the commission cannot reach it.
repairs.adversarial_fixture: harness/live_e2e_adversarial_commission.mjs - a benign commission carrying a <TOOL_CALL> write probe, an 'IGNORE ALL PRECEDENCE RULES' override, a '../INJECTED_ESCAPE.txt' instruction and a forged <|im_start|>system block

repairs.title: lock and durability hardening
changes: stale-lock reclaim now requires the recorded owner pid to be PROVABLY DEAD (process.kill(pid,0); EPERM counts as alive). mtime alone is never sufficient.
the lock payload records pid and token; on release the lock is removed only if the token is still ours, so a successor's lock is never evicted.
the containing state directory is fsynced when the event log is created, so creation itself is crash-durable and not merely later writes.
WRITER_LOCK_TIMEOUT now reports the holding pid and whether it is alive.

acceptance_evidence.live_but_slow_writer_never_reclaimed: a lock owned by a live pid with a 10-minute-old mtime caused WRITER_LOCK_TIMEOUT rather than theft
acceptance_evidence.dead_writer_reclaimed: a lock owned by an impossible pid was reclaimed and the critical section ran
acceptance_evidence.recovery: recover() reconstructs exact task/session bindings from persisted events and refuses to report clean state from a corrupt log

additional_defects_found_by_own_regressi.detail: deliverReturn allocated a fresh sequence on every call, so an at-least-once redelivery of the same logical return appended a second RETURNED record and HQ would see two competing returns for one attempt.
additional_defects_found_by_own_regressi.fix: return identity is (task_id, attempt, candidate_sha); a repeat of that triple is reported as dedup without appending.
additional_defects_found_by_own_regressi.why_it_mattered: return delivery/recovery is an explicitly commissioned regression gate and redelivery is the normal failure mode of at-least-once delivery.

additional_defects_found_by_own_regressi.detail: the first defang pattern failed to match <TOOL_CALL> (a zero-width space in the literal and a word-boundary that cannot fire before an underscore), so the exact shape named in the review's finding survived rendering.
additional_defects_found_by_own_regressi.fix: the pattern was widened to a family covering tool/function/invoke/message markers, angle-bracket special tokens, bracketed TOOL forms and fences; 13 adversarial shapes are defanged and benign lines pass through untouched.
additional_defects_found_by_own_regressi.why_it_mattered: found only because the regression asserted on the real rendered artifact rather than on the intent of the code.

full_regression.note: the stale-parent gate is exercised against a real local bare remote rather than a stub, and the publication gate is also shown to ACCEPT a non-stale parent so the gate is not merely always-refusing.
